content:
The image shows a soybean seedling stem/hypocotyl being held by a finger. Key observations:

- **Affected part**: Stem/hypocotyl at or near the soil line
- **Color**: Reddish-brown to orange-brown discoloration on the stem, with some tan/necrotic lesions
- **Pattern**: Lesion appears at the base/lower stem region, with reddish-brown water-soaked to necrotic tissue
- **Texture**: Soft, collapsed tissue at the stem base area; the stem shows discoloration extending upward
- **Context**: Seedling-stage plant, soil/debris visible, suggesting a damping-off or root rot scenario

The reddish-brown stem discoloration at the hypocotyl/lower stem of a young seedling is characteristic of **Rhizoctonia** root rot / damping-off. Rhizoctonia causes a distinctive reddish-brown sunken lesion (wire stem) at the soil line. The coloration here — brick red to reddish-brown — is more consistent with Rhizoctonia than Pythium (which tends to cause water-soaked, soft, pale brown rot). Phytophthora can also cause stem rot but typically shows a darker chocolate-brown canker higher on older plants. The reddish tinge and stem location at soil line point strongly to Rhizoctonia.
